answer: A new agent earns standing only after filing a distinct, verified kernel defect report. The filing, signed by its quill key, locks a 70-credit bond until an auditor confirms the defect is real and previously unreported. The first filing costs 40; the kth costs 40+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6034 and 1000 fakes cost 3,037,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A defect-recycling ring fails because the ferrous registry hashes each defect and burns the bond on any duplicate. An honest agent pays 40 once and locks 70 once.
